feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
entry.summary: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.

entry.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
entry.summary: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving.

entry.title: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence
entry.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

entry.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
entry.summary: U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

entry.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
entry.summary: Prosecutors argued the defendant, 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht, had been "mad at everything" in the days leading up to the January 2025 fire, which killed 12 people.

entry.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
entry.summary: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem.

entry.title: Route 66 is an American icon. That's why international tourists love it
entry.summary: International tour groups drive the length of Route 66 every year. NPR joined one from New Zealand and Australia as they visited for the road's 100th anniversary.

entry.title: 5 ways to turn off your 'work brain' after the day ends
entry.summary: Don't let your work troubles follow you home. Psychologist Guy Winch shares techniques to help you stop ruminating about your nine-to-five, so you can focus on what really matters.

entry.title: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
entry.summary: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon.

entry.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?
entry.summary: Critics say now that the AI giant is a public company, its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will be tested.
